title: Harmonize token-level SLIs, SLO thresholds, and multi-region traffic shaping dashboards
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Token-level SLI definitions, SLO thresholds, and multi-region traffic shaping rules are fragmented across dashboards and teams. This causes inconsistent alerts, unclear runbook steps during region failovers, and mismatched circuit-breaker triggers that either over-shed traffic or fail to protect capacity.

Goal: Create a harmonized set of token-level SLIs (prometheus/datadog names), agreed SLO thresholds across hosted/dedicated/private tiers, a single Grafana/Datadog dashboard that surfaces golden signals + token metrics by region/model-variant, and an operational playbook for circuit breaker/failover/load-shedding actions. Deliverables should include dashboards, monitor configs, a small automation to kick off traffic shaping, and updated runbook playbook notes for on-call.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document canonical token-level SLIs with metric names and tags (e.g., inference.token.latency_ms, inference.token.kv_cache_hitrate, inference.token.error_count) and publish to Confluence.
Agree SLO targets for tiers: Hosted (P99 token latency <= 35ms, error rate <= 0.5%), Dedicated (P99 <= 50ms, error rate <= 1%), Private (customer-negotiated) and record in SLO registry.

Implement aggregated dashboard (Grafana + Datadog dashboard links) that shows golden signals, token SLIs, circuit-breaker state, shed_rate, and per-region traffic split; dashboards must support model_variant and routing_policy filters.
Add Datadog monitors and Prometheus alerts that map to playbook severity levels (warn/escalate/SEV) and verify they fire in a canary test.

Implement and test a traffic-shaping trigger script that can (a) shift traffic regionally, (b) lower batch size, or (c) route to degraded model variant automatically via safe parameters for ramping down load.
Update the runbook with step-by-step failover and circuit-breaker remediation actions and run a tabletop drill with on-call to validate understanding.
Add a short retro and lessons learned doc after tabletop and load test, with measurable improvements to alert noise and recovery time.
All artifacts must be linked from ticket and reviewed by Reliability lead (Ruth Chen) and PM (Deepak Iyer).
notes: Trade-offs: stricter SLOs reduce customer-visible regressions but increase cost (autoscale spikes). We will favor conservative SLOs for hosted in the short term and revisit after a 4-week telemetry window.

Decision: Use Datadog for anomaly/monitoring + Grafana for operational SRE panels because Datadog synthetic monitors provide easier alert routing while Grafana supports the multivariate layout operators on time-series we need.

Instrumentation gap: token latency is emitted at the per-token layer but missing region tag in ~12% of requests; a small agent change (ENG-11105) is required to attach region and routing_policy tags. Marked as follow-up if not addressed by March 1.

Circuit breaker thresholds to try in staging: error_rate 1.5% sustained over 3m -> threshold1 (soft degrade), error_rate 3% over 3m -> open circuit and divert to fallback region. Queue length > 1200 tokens -> trigger load-shed policy. Values tuned down after load tests if false positives occur.
Load-shedding policy: prefer routing to cached-prefix or quantized model variant before hard-request drop. Only drop requests as last resort for non-SLA traffic classes.
We'll keep an audit of all route changes via the routing-control service (route-change logs) for postmortem correlation.
